title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures & Top Support Issues
author: Sarah Lin
summary: Operating procedures and canonical guidance for DevEx documentation: standardized SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site CI/CD and build operations, and a prioritized list of top support issues with canonical fixes.
content:
Overview

This page consolidates the operating procedures and canonical content patterns used by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team to produce and maintain SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, and the docs site. The goal is: consistent, discoverable, and high-quality docs that reduce Support volume and accelerate developer onboarding.

Scope
- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go)
- Quickstarts and templates (repo-level quickstarts, single-file examples)
- API examples (REST + SDK parity examples, streaming, tool-calling)
- Docs site operating procedures (build, deploy, rollback, monitoring)
- Top support issues & canonical fixes maintained as triage artifacts

Owners & Roles
- Document owner: Developer Experience (eng-developer-experience)
- Primary author: Sarah Lin (DevEx)
- Reviewers: Marcus Reed (SDK), Priya Nair (API), Ethan Cole (Docs infra)
- Publishing/CI owner: Platform Docs (eng-platform)

Standards & Conventions
1) Tone and audience
- Audience: software engineers integrating Redwood Inference into products and prototypes.
- Tone: direct, example-driven, minimal hand-holding for advanced topics; more hand-holding in quickstarts.

2) File & page naming
- Use short, dash-separated names. Example: python-quickstart-auth.md -> "python-quickstart-auth".
- Page titles: Title Case, concise.

3) Content structure (required sections for each page)
- Short intro (1-3 sentences)
- When to use this page (bullet list)
- Prerequisites (tools, permissions, API keys)
- Step-by-step instructions / code samples
- Troubleshooting / common errors
- Ownership & review info
- Related pages / links

SDK Guide Template (required fields)
- Title
- Quick summary (1 sentence)
- Supported languages & versions (e.g., Python >=3.10, TS >=4.5)
- Installation (pip/npm/go get) with exact commands and example package versions
- Quick example (3-6 lines) demonstrating authentication + basic call
- Advanced patterns: batching, streaming, function/tool-calls, retries, pagination
- Configuration & environment variables (list key names and purpose)
- Tests & CI hints (how to run example tests locally)
- API parity table (SDK method -> REST endpoint)

Example: Minimal Python SDK quickstart snippet\n```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(prompt="Summarize the release notes in one sentence")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts & Templates (how to create)
- Quickstart target time-to-success: 10 minutes for a developer with Python/TS experience.
- Template types: single-file demo, repo-level tutorial with tests, interactive notebook.
- Each quickstart must include: setup script (install deps), sample app, instructions for local run, expected output assertion(s).
- Place repo-level quickstarts under: /quickstarts/<language>/<name>/README.md with a LICENSE and tests/.

API Examples Guidelines
- Every REST endpoint referenced on the docs site must have a matching SDK example for Python and TypeScript.
- Use real-ish but redacted example data (no PII).
- Prefer complete request/response pairs; include headers and minimal auth examples.
- Streaming examples must show both server-side behavior and client-side consumption patterns.

Docs Site Operating Procedures (CI/CD)
1) Branching & content workflow
- Author creates feature branch: docs/<area>/<short-desc> (e.g., docs/sdk/python-batching)
- Open PR against main/docs; include checklist (lint, link-check, unit examples)
- Required approvals: 1 reviewer from DevEx + 1 from relevant SDK owner for SDK/API changes.

2) Build & Preview
- Docs site built by CI job: docs-site/build (runs Hugo static build + link check + code snippet validation).
- Preview environments: netlify/docs-preview/<pr-number> (automatic deploy on PR).
- Build SLO: 99% successful builds over 30 days; failures create an alert in #docs-ops.

3) Publishing
- Merge to main triggers Canary deploy to docs-canary.redwood.ai for 2 hours. If no regressions reported, promote to production.
- Promotion job tags release with semantic tag docs-YYYYMMDD-<short>.

4) Rollback
- If a regression is detected post-promotion, use the docs-site/rollback job to redeploy the previous production tag. Documented steps:
  1) Identify bad tag from deploy logs.
  2) Run: `kubectl -n docs deploy docs-site --image=docs-site:<previous-tag>` or trigger CI rollback pipeline.
  3) Post a status update to #docs-ops and the PR for visibility.

5) Monitoring & Alerts
- Key metrics: build_success_rate (SLO 99%), preview_deploy_latency (median < 90s), production_404_rate (SLO 0.1%).
- Alerts: build_failure (on first failure), preview_deploy_failed, production_404_spike (5xx > 0.5% in 5m).
- Alert routing: primary to #docs-ops, pager to oncall-infra for production degradations.

Maintenance & Review Cadence
- Major content audit (full quickstarts and SDK guides): quarterly.
- Minor reviews (API example parity): monthly, automated diff against API spec.
- Deprecation policy: mark pages deprecated 60 days before removal, add notice banner and redirect page.

Top Support Issues (2025-2026) & Canonical Fixes
1) "Authentication failed: invalid API key"
- Symptom: 401 from REST or SDK init error.
- Root cause: using org-scoped key vs project key or missing REDWOOD_API_KEY in environment.
- Canonical fix: instruct user to create a project key in Console > API keys, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; provide command:
  - `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx`
  - `# For Windows (PowerShell): $Env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk-xxxx'`

2) "Streaming responses hang / never finish"
- Symptom: client receives initial frame(s) but does not see EOS.
- Root cause: client-side stream handler not consuming event type 'done' or missing backpressure handling.
- Canonical fix: include robust streaming consumer sample for each SDK; add note about socket timeouts and recommend a 60s keepalive.

3) "Inconsistent SDK vs REST output (parity)"
- Symptom: different tokenization/stop behavior between REST example and SDK call.
- Root cause: missing explicit decode/encoding or default model params differing between examples.
- Canonical fix: update examples to include explicit parameters (model, temperature, stop tokens) and add parity test in CI which runs both examples and compares normalized outputs.

4) "Docs build fails due to code snippet lint error"
- Symptom: CI fails link-check or snippet-linter job.
- Root cause: new code example introduces an unsupported syntax or missing dependency.
- Canonical fix: maintain per-language snippet containers and add a pre-commit hook that runs snippet validation locally. Document: `make docs-validate`.

5) "Quickstart environment mismatch (missing system deps)"
- Symptom: users report quickstart failing due to missing system libs (e.g., libpq, ffmpeg).
- Root cause: quickstart assumes a container but user runs on bare host.
- Canonical fix: add a troubleshooting prereqs section listing system dependencies, include Docker dev container for reference.

6) "SDK install fails / version conflicts"
- Symptom: pip/npm install fails with dependency conflict.
- Root cause: example pinned to older dependency or user's global env conflicts.
- Canonical fix: recommend virtualenv/nvm usage in quickstart, include pinned example in pyproject.toml/package.json and `pip install -r requirements.txt` instructions.

7) "Rate limit / 429 errors in quickstart"
- Symptom: Developers get 429 on sample workloads.
- Root cause: free-tier limits, shared test account, or missing retry logic.
- Canonical fix: show exponential backoff example in SDK guides and note default rate limits in prerequisites; include guidance on requesting higher quota.

8) "Mismatched examples for function/tool-calling"
- Symptom: examples show different JSON schema for tool definitions across pages.
- Root cause: historical edits across multiple pages.
- Canonical fix: centralize tool schema in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/tool-schemas and use include mechanism for pages; run a monthly linter to validate tool schema references.

9) "Search not finding updated pages"
- Symptom: search index lag after publishing.
- Root cause: search re-index job failure or misconfigured cache TTL.
- Canonical fix: run `scripts/reindex-search --force` and monitor reindex job; increase cache TTL for static assets when frequent updates are expected.

10) "Deprecated API examples still present"
- Symptom: old examples surface in search.
- Root cause: missing deprecation banners and redirects.
- Canonical fix: apply deprecation banner template and add redirect from old URL to replacement; remove from active navigation only after 60 days.

Canonical Fix Playbook (how to update this doc)
- If an issue above occurs 3x in a 30-day window, create an RFC in eng-developer-experience and update this page with incident notes, a permanent fix, and add a link to the postmortem.
- Maintain a single source-of-truth examples repo: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-examples. All SDK/quickstart PRs must include CI-green status from that repo.

Appendix: Useful commands & CI jobs
- Local preview: `make docs-serve` (starts local Hugo server at http://localhost:1313)
- Validate snippets: `make docs-validate`
- Force reindex: `scripts/reindex-search --force`
- Trigger docs rollback (CI): `ci/pipelines/rollback-docs --tag <previous-tag>`
